findings.title: Candidate: double-leading-slash path is forwarded to origin unchanged (no malicious payload bypass confirmed)
findings.impact: Path normalization differs between WAF and some origins (UNC/backslash semantics). No SQLi/XSS payload reached the origin in this audit; severity depends on origin server semantics.

findings.title: Candidate: Content-Encoding gzip is decoded only one layer; gzip(gzip(SQLi)) is forwarded to the origin intact

evidence.control: Single-layer gzip with the same payload is 403 (blocked); double layer is 200 and origin body is gzip(gzip("q=1 union select 1")).

findings.impact: If the origin/app stack recursively decompresses (or forwards the body to an app that does), the SQLi payload is not inspected. Confirmation requires a recursive-decompression origin; current mock origin does not decode, so this stays candidate.
findings.fix_hint: Decompress to a bounded depth (reject remaining gzip magic after one decode) and reject multi-valued Content-Encoding.

notes: Manual re-test of 7 attack payloads (path traversal / XSS / SQLi) on path variants returned 403 and origin log empty. T2-05..T2-15 were not completed by the track worker (model transport failure); they remain untested. Manual T2-X tests: multipart SQLi 403, single gzip 403, double gzip 200 (candidate T2-C2), UTF-16 JSON 403, duplicate JSON key 403, raw chunked 400.
